transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Liam (PM), Ava (Eng Mgr), Priya (SWE), Diego (SRE), Sophie (ProdOps), Marcus (Release), Evelyn (QA)
---
Summary:
- Postmortem and launch readiness check for Q3 roadmap slice: launch features v2.1 (routing policies, KV cache improvements, canary rollout).
- Identified outstanding items around canary gating, perf regressions on long-context traces, and runbook updates.
- Agreed owners and near-term dates for smoke tests, canary docs, and incident playbook updates.
---
Topics: launch readiness, incident review, performance regression, canary plan, runbooks, release timeline
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: Okay let's kick off, uh, thanks everyone for joining, want to make sure we cover the post-mortem highlights and then walk through the launch readiness checklist. We got 75 minutes, so I'll keep time.
[00:22] Ava: yep thanks Liam, quick note — engineering did a last-minute revert on the streaming kernel change which fixed the mem spike, but we still see a throughput delta on long sequences.
[00:37] Priya: yeah so the regression shows up at ~32k tokens, the KV cash - uh K-V cash - caching paths, it falls back to a slower codepath, looks like a mismatch in kernel selection heuristics. I filed RD-441.
[00:55] Diego: SRE did a repro, wasn't stable on the first run, the traces had occasional GC stalls from the comms layer; could be protobuf marshalling, maybe the batching service.
[01:15] Marcus: timeline question - are we still targeting 2026-06-25 for the canary start? or do we push a week given these perf things?
[01:26] Liam: I'd prefer to keep the 25th target but with tight gating; if Priya's smoke tests pass and Marcus's canary gates are explicit then we can go. We need clear stop conditions.
[01:40] Evelyn: QA needs the smoke suite to include long-context regressions and a couple of negative tests for fallback models; last time the embedding latency spiked under certain batch mixes.
[02:00] Priya: noted — I'll add long-context test cases, including 30k and 50k token replay of the Tesoro dataset, also include KV cache priming.
[02:20] Ava: also we should check compilation kernel flags — sometimes the auto-kernel selector chooses an older path on A100s for sequences > 16k, that might be the cause.
[02:36] Diego: can we get perf profiles attached to RD-441? I want CPU+GPU timelines and the batch aggregator logs.
[02:46] Priya: yes, I'll upload perf flamegraphs and nvprof outputs, though nvprof naming might be messy, sometimes it shows 'nvprof' as n-v-prop in the traces.
[03:05] Liam: ok onto the postmortem: quick recap from Sophie?
[03:12] Sophie: Postmortem high level: unexpeced mem growth during a high QPS run triggered by streaming kernel change + unexpected fallback on some shard types; customers saw elevated latency for ~18 minutes; no data loss. We recommended revert + hotfixed autoscaler thresholds.
[03:36] Ava: we also found incomplete health checks on the new pod template which let a degraded instance remain in rotation longer than it should. That was the main reliability vector.
[03:50] Marcus: on the rollback - were the rollout metrics sufficient? did we have the right dashboards to detect the regression earlier?
[04:00] Diego: alerting was tuned for error rates and not for small latency degradations; need a latency SLO-based alert to trigger on p95 for critical routes.
[04:18] Evelyn: QA wasn't added to the canary review signoff list - we should add QA and ProdOps to the gating approvals.
[04:31] Liam: agreed, new canary checklist will require QA signoff and a green smoke suite, plus Perf attached.
[04:45] Priya: implementation note - the KV cache priming is non-deterministic in current harness; I'll make the priming deterministic for the smoke so we get reproducible traces.
[05:00] Marcus: docs - Marcus will put the canary checklist in Confluence with explicit SLA gates e.g., p95 < 120ms for routing, error rate < 0.1% and mem delta < 15%.
[05:20] Ava: and also include fallback model policy: fallback only when token cost exceeds threshold or latency spikes, we need explicit routing fallback thresholds in the doc.
[05:35] Diego: runbook changes - the incident playbook needs a step that says 'if mem growth > X% in 10 minutes, remove node from rotation and start hotspot capture'.
[05:50] Liam: nice. Sophie can you capture that as a new runbook bullet?
[05:58] Sophie: yeah I'll add it after the call.
[06:05] Liam: good, shifting to release timing - we have the marketing/ops freeze on 06-24, so pushing beyond 06-25 will likely slip Q3 comms. We can choose to soft launch to a small set of customers if we have the gates.
[06:22] Priya: soft launch seems prudent - do 2% of traffic with strict routing to dedicated pool, fallback to hosted compatible shim.
[06:35] Marcus: that requires routing policy changes - can be done but needs config review with infra; I'll own the config change plus rollback plan.
[06:47] Ava: we should test the config in a staging canary mirror first.
[06:55] Diego: I'll provision a mirror at 1% qps to match load shape.
[07:05] Evelyn: QA will run a small exploratory session during the mirror to validate user flows.
[07:15] Liam: ok next - monitoring improvements, Diego?
[07:20] Diego: add histograms for live kv cache latency per shard, and emit a synthetic trace when a kernel fallback happens to help correlate. Also we should add a metric for scheduler backpressure.
[07:36] Priya: small callout: kernel heuristics currently use avg sequence length over 1000 requests; we should make the window smaller so we adapt faster to long-context bursts.
[07:50] Ava: agree, change window to 100 requests for experimental, Priya can test.
[07:58] Priya: yep will try that on staging.
[08:05] Liam: action items recap (quick): Priya smoke tests + perf uploads, Marcus canary doc, Ava runbook updates, Diego load tests + metrics. Dates?
[08:16] Priya: 06-21 for smoke.
[08:19] Marcus: 06-22 for canary doc.
[08:21] Ava: 06-20 for runbook.
[08:24] Diego: 06-19 for load tests.
[08:30] Liam: perfect. Any blockers?
[08:33] Marcus: infra quota - we might need temporary extra GPUs for the load test window, Diego can request.
[08:40] Diego: noted, I'll open request today.
[08:45] Sophie: I'll schedule a quick canary dry-run meeting on 06-23 to validate checklist.
[08:50] Liam: schedule it; include on-call, SRE, QA and release eng.
[09:00] Evelyn: one more QA note - please include real customer prompt sets for regression, not synthetic ones; synthetic missed a tokenization edge case last time.
[09:18] Priya: we'll pull anonymized prompts from the bench and scrub PII, ok.
[09:30] Liam: good. Any other risks?
[09:34] Ava: supply chain for dedicated nodes - our partner region has limited A100 stock, might affect capacity for dedicated canary. We might need to use mixed instance types.
[09:48] Marcus: if we use mixed types, update performance baselines and gating thresholds accordingly.
[09:56] Diego: and add instance-type metadata to all perf traces so we can filter.
[10:04] Liam: final recap: keep target 06-25 for canary start; owners and dates as discussed; dry-run 06-23; stop conditions and gates documented by Marcus; smoke results by Priya; runbook updated by Ava; load tests by Diego.
[10:22] Liam: I'll follow up with an email summary and calendar invites for the dry-run and post-decision sync.
[10:30] Sophie: I'll attach the postmortem doc and the incident timeline to the ticket after the call.
[10:40] Marcus: I'll also add the canary checklist link in the ticket.
[10:50] Liam: excellent, thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
